content: Clomiphene is a medication prescribed to stimulate ovulation in women who are unable to produce eggs but wish to conceive. It belongs to a class of drugs known as ovulatory stimulants and functions in a manner similar to estrogen, a hormone that promotes the development and release of eggs from the ovaries. Clomiphene is available in tablet form and is taken orally. Typically, it is administered once daily for a duration of five days, starting around the fifth day of the menstrual cycle. Follow the instructions provided on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Do not alter the dosage or frequency of the medication without your doctor’s approval. In addition to its primary use, clomiphene may also be prescribed for other conditions, such as male infertility, menstrual irregularities, fibrocystic breast disease, or persistent lactation. If you are considering using clomiphene for any of these conditions, discuss the potential risks with your doctor. This medication may also have other off-label uses; consult your healthcare provider or pharmacist for further information. Before starting clomiphene, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to clomiphene or other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and over-the-counter medications, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver disease, ovarian cysts (excluding those caused by polycystic ovary syndrome), uterine fibroids, abnormal vaginal bleeding, pituitary tumors, or thyroid or adrenal disorders. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, inform your doctor immediately. Should you become pregnant while taking clomiphene, contact your doctor without delay. Be aware that clomiphene may cause blurred vision. Avoid driving or operating machinery, particularly in low-light conditions, until you understand how the medication affects you. Additionally, clomiphene increases the likelihood of multiple pregnancies (e.g., twins or more). Discuss the risks associated with multiple pregnancies with your doctor. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while taking clomiphene. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is nearly time for your next scheduled dose, contact your doctor for guidance. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Clomiphene may cause side effects. Common, less severe side effects include: Flushing or a sensation of warmth Nausea or upset stomach Vomiting Breast tenderness or discomfort Headache Abnormal vaginal bleeding Some side effects, though rare, may be serious. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: Blurred vision Visual disturbances, such as spots, flashes, or double vision Abdominal or pelvic pain Abdominal swelling Unexplained weight gain Shortness of breath Prolonged use of clomiphene may increase the risk of ovarian cancer. It is generally not recommended to use this medication for more than six treatment cycles. Discuss the risks of long-term use with your doctor. If you experience any unusual or concerning symptoms while taking clomiphene, notify your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store clomiphene in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Symptoms of overdose may include: Nausea or upset stomach Vomiting Hot flashes Blurred vision or visual disturbances Blind spots Abdominal swelling Abdominal or pelvic pain It is important to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and undergo any recommended laboratory tests to monitor your response to clomiphene. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Clomiphene is sold under the brand names Clomid® and Serophene®.
